premise: Deer's antlers drop off in winter and he worries he isn't himself; by summer new ones have grown, and Bird perches in them.
inspiration: Kipling's Just So stories (how the animal got its feature), told truly and turned toward reassurance: what goes away can come back bigger.
lesson: You are still you, even when you change.
learning: Deer lose their antlers every year and grow new ones

en-US.title: Deer's New Antlers
en-US.text: One winter morning, Deer {deer:pulse} gave his head a little shake, and his antlers came loose and dropped into the snow, {sfx:plop} plop, plop, as easy as two leaves. [gasps] My antlers! Deer {deer:tint #FFB3C6} went pink. Without them, am I still me? Rabbit {rabbit:hop} hopped all around him. [giggles] You look like you to me. Just lighter! Bird {bird:float loop 0.3} landed on his head. Don't worry, he sang. Every deer loses his antlers in winter. New ones will grow. [curious] Really? said Deer. And they did. In spring, two little bumps. Then two soft, velvety branches. By summer, two big new antlers, {deer:glow} taller than before. [happily] Bird {bird:hop} tried them out straight away. Perfect, he said. A tree that walks!

es-ES.title: Las astas nuevas de Ciervo
es-ES.text: Una mañana de invierno, Ciervo {deer:pulse} sacudió un poco la cabeza, y sus astas se soltaron y cayeron en la nieve, {sfx:plop} plof, plof, tan fácil como dos hojas. [gasps] ¡Mis astas! Ciervo {deer:tint #FFB3C6} se puso colorado. Sin ellas, ¿sigo siendo yo? Conejo {rabbit:hop} saltó a su alrededor. [giggles] Yo te veo igual. ¡Solo que más ligero! Pájaro {bird:float loop 0.3} se posó en su cabeza. No te preocupes, cantó. A todos los ciervos se les caen las astas en invierno. Te crecerán otras. [curious] ¿De verdad?, dijo Ciervo. Y así fue. En primavera, dos bultitos. Luego dos ramitas suaves, como de terciopelo. En verano, dos astas nuevas y grandes, {deer:glow} más altas que antes. [happily] Pájaro {bird:hop} las probó enseguida. Perfectas, dijo. ¡Un árbol que camina!
